title: Provider-neutral harness seam and the dsh adapter
summary: Adds a provider-neutral `harness` module — a `Harness` trait, a `CommandRunner` seam, plain-data result types and an in-memory fake — plus the first concrete adapter, `dsh_harness`, which runs `dsh --profile headless --json -` through a runner, parses newline-delimited JSON events, reads changed files and head from git, and reports capabilities by probing `--version`, headless `--help` and `--dump-config`. Nothing in the neutral module names a harness or a model vendor; the adapter is the only place that does, and a test enforces that split.

lanes.label: Neutral harness seam
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/harness
lanes.summary: Provider-neutral trait, command spec, result types and the in-memory test double. Names no harness and no model vendor.

lanes.label: dsh adapter
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/dsh_harness.rs
lanes.summary: The first concrete Harness: builds the dsh command, parses its JSONL events, reads git state, and probes capabilities.

lanes.label: Command runner
lanes.subtitle: process boundary
lanes.summary: The seam that actually starts processes. The adapter never spawns anything itself; the runner does.

lanes.label: External tools
lanes.subtitle: dsh and git
lanes.summary: The dsh binary and git, reached only through the runner with an explicit environment.

lanes.label: Tests and fixtures
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/tests
lanes.summary: Recorded dsh runs, help and dump-config fixtures, the fake-run integration test, and the neutrality scanner.

nodes.label: Harness trait
nodes.subtitle: run / capabilities
nodes.summary: The seam between the factory and an external coding harness. `run` takes a `CommandRunner` and a `HarnessTask`; `capabilities` reports what the harness can do as Supported, Unsupported or Unknown.

nodes.label: CommandSpec / CommandOutput
nodes.subtitle: program, args, env, stdin, timeout
nodes.summary: Plain data describing one command and its result. The environment is the complete child environment; nothing is inherited.

nodes.label: HarnessResult / Usage / Actor
nodes.subtitle: plain data for the journal
nodes.summary: What a run produced: actor, session id, final message, outcome, exit, changed files, branch, head commit, summed token usage and cost. Serializes directly into the journal.

nodes.label: build_prompt / question_line
nodes.subtitle: rules + QUESTION: marker
nodes.summary: Builds the task prompt with the four rules appended, and reads a question from the last non-blank line of a final message when it carries the `QUESTION:` prefix.

nodes.label: FakeRunner / FakeHarness
nodes.subtitle: scripted replay, no process
nodes.summary: In-memory doubles that replay scripted answers and record every command and task as plain data, so a full run can be exercised without starting a process.

nodes.label: DshHarness
nodes.subtitle: impl Harness for dsh
nodes.summary: The concrete adapter. Validates the task, checks the tree is clean, records head and branch, runs dsh, parses events, re-reads status and head, and refuses a run that moved head.

nodes.label: DshConfig
nodes.subtitle: program, env, pinned version
nodes.summary: How to reach the dsh binary: its program, its complete child environment, and the version `--version` must report (0.2.0-rc.2).

nodes.label: build_command / git commands
nodes.subtitle: dsh --profile headless --json -
nodes.summary: Pure builders for the agent command and the three git commands (status, head, branch). Git gets only PATH, HOME and GIT_* so no credential reaches it.

nodes.label: parse_events
nodes.subtitle: JSONL → Parsed
nodes.summary: Reads newline-delimited JSON events: session id, final message, summed step usage, and the first turn_end whose reason is not `completed`. A non-JSON line is an error naming its line number.

nodes.label: parse_changed_files / parse_head / parse_branch
nodes.subtitle: porcelain -z, rev-parse
nodes.summary: Turns `git status --porcelain=v1 -z` into a sorted, deduplicated file list including a rename's original path, and reads head and branch from rev-parse.

nodes.label: probe_version / probe_headless / probe_stop_hook
nodes.subtitle: --version, --help, --dump-config
nodes.summary: Three probes that report capabilities rather than assume them. A probe that cannot run is Unknown, never Unsupported. The stop-hook probe reads the profile dump for the message-check plugin row.

nodes.label: message_check_in
nodes.subtitle: reads the plugin row
nodes.summary: Parses a `--dump-config` dump for the `@open-software-factory/osf-dsh-plugin` row and reports Enabled, Absent, Disabled or Conditional, preferring the strongest state when several rows name it.

nodes.label: CommandRunner
nodes.subtitle: starts the process
nodes.summary: The trait that actually runs a command with exactly its env, workdir and stdin, kills the process tree at the timeout, and answers TimedOut. The adapter only ever calls it.

nodes.label: dsh binary
nodes.subtitle: headless profile
nodes.summary: The external coding harness. Run as `dsh --profile headless --json -` with the prompt on stdin; prints newline-delimited JSON events on stdout.

nodes.label: git
nodes.subtitle: status, rev-parse
nodes.summary: Reads the repository state around a run: the changed-file list, the head commit and the branch. Reached with a minimal environment that carries no credential.

nodes.label: Recorded dsh runs
nodes.subtitle: created file, question, no credential
nodes.summary: Real recorded JSONL runs: a created file, several question shapes, and a missing-credential turn failure. They pin the parser against what dsh actually prints.

nodes.label: version / help / dump-config
nodes.subtitle: probe inputs
nodes.summary: The pinned version text, the headless help, and a full profile dump used to exercise the capability probes and the message-check reader.

nodes.label: harness_fake_run.rs
nodes.subtitle: full run through the fakes
nodes.summary: Drives a complete run and a capability report through the trait objects with the in-memory fakes, asserting the exact command sequence, the environment split, and the serialized result.

nodes.label: harness_neutral.rs
nodes.subtitle: scanner that can fail
nodes.summary: Asserts the neutral harness folder names no supported agent, no container word and no model vendor, and proves the scanner can fail by pointing it at the dsh adapter.

edges.label: impl Harness
edges.summary: The adapter implements the neutral trait, so the factory can hold a `Box<dyn Harness>` and never name dsh.

edges.label: run(CommandSpec)
edges.summary: Every process the adapter needs — dsh, git, the probes — goes through the runner. The adapter starts nothing itself.

edges.label: spawn
edges.summary: The runner starts dsh with the prompt on stdin and the configured environment.

edges.label: spawn
edges.summary: The runner starts git for status, head and branch, with only PATH, HOME and GIT_* in the environment.
The adapter builds the agent command and the git commands from its config before handing them to the runner.
The adapter parses the JSONL stdout into session id, final message, usage and turn failure.
The adapter reads changed files, head and branch before and after the run, and refuses a run that moved head.
capabilities() runs the three probes and reports each as Supported, Unsupported or Unknown.
The stop-hook probe reads the profile dump through message_check_in to decide whether a plugin checks messages at the end of a turn.
The adapter builds the prompt with the rules and reads the question marker back out of the final message.
The adapter assembles the plain-data result the journal records.
FakeRunner implements CommandRunner by replaying scripted outputs and recording every command.
FakeHarness implements Harness by replaying scripted results and recording every task.
The integration test drives the real adapter with a FakeRunner, asserting the exact six-command sequence and the environment split.
The test feeds the recorded runs through the adapter and asserts the parsed result.
The capability tests feed the version, help and dump-config fixtures through the probes.
The scanner reads the neutral harness folder and asserts it names no agent, container word or model vendor.
The scanner is pointed at the dsh adapter to prove it can fail, since that file does name a model vendor.
